<meta>continues from previous page: and we will laugh to our hearts' content,</meta>

<term>EV.</term> <note>Eubulus</note> What birds do I see here? <term>CA.</term> <note>Catharina</note> It is the patriarch of the college. Do not withdraw yourself; they have already finished drinking; sit down for a little while; when he has departed we shall chat in our usual manner. <term>EV.</term> Come, I will comply with you, which I was unwilling to do before. Now we are alone, tell the whole story, for I would prefer to learn it from you. <term>CA.</term> Out of so many friends, whom I thought were very many indeed, I now feel that there was none who gave me more prudent or mature counsel than you, the youngest of them all. <term>EV.</term> But how did you overcome the affection of your parents? <term>CA.</term> First, by the wicked exhortations of the monks and nuns: then also by my own: the mind of my mother was weakened by prayers and flatteries: my father could in no way be pushed. Finally, with every engine of persuasion moved against him, he too was conquered and overwhelmed rather than consenting. It was done during the drinking; they threatened a horrible evil and destruction if he should deny his own daughter to Christ as His bride. <term>EV.</term> O the wickedness of those fools! What happened then? <term>CA.</term> I was kept at home in secret for three days: meanwhile some women of that college were always present, whom they call <term>Conversas</term> <gloss>Lay Sisters or Converts</gloss>, adding courage with their exhortations so that I might persist in my holy purpose, and taking anxious care lest any of my kinswomen or companions should come to me, who might seem likely to change my mind. In the meantime, the garments were being prepared, and other things pertaining to the feast. <term>EV.</term> What was your state of mind meanwhile? Did you waver at all? <term>CA.</term> No, but I suffered something so horrendous that I would prefer to die ten times over than to endure it again. <term>EV.</term> I pray you, what is that? <term>CA.</term> I cannot speak of it. <term>EV.</term> Whatever you tell me, you will be telling to your friend. <term>CA.</term> Do you promise silence? <term>EV.</term> I would have provided that even if you had stipulated nothing. As if you did not yet know me.

<summary>Catharina confesses to Eubulus that her parents were coerced into allowing her to join the convent through the aggressive tactics and threats of monks and nuns. She describes being sequestered and pressured by lay sisters while preparations for her initiation were made.</summary>
<keywords>monasticism, parental consent, religious coercion, Eubulus, Catharina, Lay Sisters, spiritual manipulation</keywords>
